C01.signature: Volunteers give pairs self-contained shared openings, sometimes initial reciprocal turns, while retaining the routine. Removing unequal prior context should improve entry and useful speech after pairing. Requires comparable accessible prompts and feasible preparation; attendance and public labels remain optional.
C01.reason: Agreed family preserved. All eleven openings reset shared context and test entry/usefulness; timing and familiarity strata refine the archived entry mechanism.

C02.signature: Volunteers place one next-session date and task prominently on existing paper, distribute it at sessions and sometimes recap it. Temporal identification should reduce stale-task answers and clarification work. Requires timely task selection, understandable dates and offline copies; earlier, blank and receipt-coded answers bound the account.
C02.reason: The eleven members share single-task temporal identification. H3-F03 supplies the intervention and H3-F06 the information-confusion investigation. Reusable layout alone is not H3-F04 topic-pack reuse. Advance acquisition across missing handoffs is assessed separately in C03.

C03.signature: Volunteers prepublish multiple independent tasks indexed by future dates; learners retain the paper and select the relevant task after absences without another weekly handoff. Requires advance topic commitments, understandable dates and retained or session-replacement copies. Predict fewer stale selections and lower recurring information work, counting setup costs.
C03.reason: All four members supply future information before a possible missed handoff. That acquisition path differs from handing out one next task or volunteers reusing packs; novelty is local to the incomplete archive, not the number or shape of cards. P009 tests recovery with hypothetical return dates. Outcomes remain untested.

C04.signature: Volunteers combine self-contained prompts, optional supports, balanced roles or timed turns and sometimes reversible quick pairing. These additive operations target entry delay and unequal speaking opportunity; faster starts or more speech must also improve reported usefulness. Assumes acceptable prompts and affordable coordination within the session.
C04.reason: Agreed four-member bundle retained. No member asserts an isolated interaction beyond the archived components. C12 may add adaptive feedback, but its distinct benefit is not specified adequately.

C05.signature: Partners alternately supply content unknown to the other, using complementary scenario sheets or private personal/invented examples; listeners discover it, sometimes retell it, and roles reverse. Reciprocal informational dependence should ease entry and support useful speech versus shared content. Assumes comfortable accessible subjects and feasible materials.
C05.reason: Agreed three-member family retained. Each speaker becomes a needed source; allocated turns and shared fresh prompts alone do not create that dependence. Personal versus split-sheet content is compatible with the same path.

C06.signature: Participants prepare one enduring invitation for their next attendance, bringing a question or personal material; unprepared arrivals use immediate examples. Removing changing task identity should reduce obsolete-task answers and planning/clarification work while supplying conversation. Requires continued motivation, suitability and sufficient offline access.
C06.reason: Agreed two-member family and local novelty retained. Stable preparation eliminates version succession rather than improving version selection. P005 adds an unverified pickup dependency; that does not change the shared mechanism.

C07.signature: At each speaker-role handoff, a fresh scenario and optional supports reset shared context while alternating roles allocate access. Context reset should make turns usable and roles ensure participation. Compare cards, roles, both and usual practice for usefulness beyond either component; assume feasible cards and accepted supports.
C07.reason: Agreed singleton retained. The explicit context-at-handoff interaction is distinct from additive C04 and the other component interactions; effectiveness remains speculative.

C08.signature: Partners explain a dated paper task, check the explanation against its card/example and correct mismatches. The date anchors the correct version while reciprocal checking exposes interpretation errors; retained paper supports later recall. Component comparisons test complementary gains. Requires accurate brief checks and offline access.
C08.reason: All three members share version-anchored peer checking. P008 additionally observes later recall, without contradicting the common path. H3-F03 supplies dated paper and recap; H3-F06 does not supply interpretation checking or the claimed interaction. Workload logging alone does not make it an equivalent archive mechanism.

C09.signature: Pairs combine fresh shared context with privately chosen language scaffolds. Resetting history and making demands usable should jointly improve useful speaking and reduce changes beyond summed component gains. Compare baseline, restart, scaffold and both; require optional reusable supports within existing resources.
C09.reason: Agreed singleton retained. The context-by-support interaction has a distinct component-controlled prediction; success remains untested.

C10.signature: Pairs cross private scaffolds with protected reciprocal turns: scaffolds make available airtime useful and turns ensure opportunities to use them. Compare scaffold-only, turns-only, combined and incumbent conditions for gains beyond summed separate gains and lower imbalance; require useful voluntary supports and feasible timing.
C10.reason: Agreed singleton retained. This support-by-airtime prediction differs from context-by-support and context-at-role-handoff interactions.

C11.signature: Pairs independently vary fresh/familiar scenarios and optional/existing supports. Context should affect first-exchange latency; support should improve usefulness with fresh context held fixed. Comparable scenarios, private choices and feasible observation are required.
C11.reason: Agreed singleton retained. The independent-effects discriminator differs from interaction claims and sharpens the archived opportunity-versus-suitability question.

C12.signature: Partners use optional scaffolds and two six-minute speaker roles, then jointly decide whether to change support. The proposed continuous adjustment depends on a reliable usefulness signal. The supplied probe compares supported and usual rounds for balance and usefulness, without contrasting adaptive and fixed support.
C12.reason: The explicit after-round support-choice operation supports mechanism classification, despite an aspirational capability label. Archived turns and scaffolds match the partial action; F05 does not provide the missing adjustment signal. Whether feedback adds a distinct causal path to C04 remains uncertain; Distill loses that relation.

C13.signature: Volunteers measure temporal/source recognition separately from task identification: correct next-date answers, on-sheet lookup, or correct-panel viewing are compared with task errors or unaided answers. Errors despite a correct temporal/source cue limit a pure version-confusion account. Requires separate consistent coding; this cannot isolate comprehension from attention or recall.
C13.reason: P001 Z2, P007 Z2 and P010 A2 each specify this conditional diagnostic contrast. Calendar versus single-sheet presentation is secondary to that shared question. Unlike P009 A2, their distinguishing prediction concerns errors remaining despite recognized cues, rather than recovery at a hypothetical return date. Archive F06 lacks that explicit discriminator.
